title: Grade 11 Mathematics — Straight Lines
description: Slope, equations of lines, distance, angles between lines
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The slope (gradient) of a line passing through (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) is:
questions.explanation: Slope m = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁) = rise/run. The slope measures the steepness — change in y per unit change in x. A horizontal line has m=0; vertical line has undefined slope.

questions.question: The equation of a line with slope m and y-intercept c is:
options: Both A and C (different but equivalent forms)
questions.explanation: Slope-intercept form: y = mx + c. Here m = slope, c = y-intercept (where line crosses y-axis). Point-slope form: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Standard form: ax + by + c = 0.

questions.question: Find the slope of the line 3x + 4y − 12 = 0.
questions.explanation: Rearrange to y = mx + c: 4y = −3x + 12 → y = −(3/4)x + 3. Slope m = −3/4.

questions.question: Two lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are:
questions.explanation: Parallel lines: same slope (m₁ = m₂), different y-intercepts. Perpendicular lines: m₁ × m₂ = −1 (slopes are negative reciprocals). Coincident lines: same slope AND same y-intercept.

questions.question: The equation of the line through (2,3) with slope 4 is:
questions.explanation: Point-slope form: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). y − 3 = 4(x − 2) = 4x − 8. y = 4x − 5.

questions.question: The distance from point (x₁, y₁) to line ax + by + c = 0 is:
questions.explanation: Distance from point (x₁,y₁) to line ax+by+c=0: d = |ax₁+by₁+c| / √(a²+b²). The absolute value ensures positive distance.

questions.question: Find the distance from point (3, 4) to line 3x − 4y + 5 = 0.
Two perpendicular lines have slopes m₁ and m₂. The condition is:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines: m₁ × m₂ = −1. If m₁ = 2, then m₂ = −1/2. Exception: a horizontal line (m=0) is perpendicular to a vertical line (undefined slope).

questions.question: The intercept form of a line with x-intercept a and y-intercept b is:
questions.explanation: Intercept form: x/a + y/b = 1. Verify: at y=0, x=a ✓; at x=0, y=b ✓. This form is useful when intercepts are given.

questions.question: The angle θ between two lines with slopes m₁ and m₂ satisfies:
questions.explanation: Angle between lines: tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| (use absolute value for acute angle). If 1 + m₁m₂ = 0, lines are perpendicular (θ = 90°).

questions.question: Lines 2x + 3y = 6 and 4x + 6y = 12 are:
questions.explanation: 2x+3y=6 and 4x+6y=12: divide second by 2: 2x+3y=6 — same equation. Coincident lines (infinitely many solutions).

questions.question: The x-intercept of the line 2x + 3y = 12 is:
A line passing through (0, 0) with slope 3/4 has equation:
options: A and C are the same
questions.explanation: y = mx + c with c=0 (passes through origin): y = (3/4)x → 4y = 3x. Options A and C are the same (both correct).

questions.question: Three points A(1,2), B(3,6), C(2,4) are collinear. This is verified by:
options: Slopes AB = slope BC = slope AC (all equal)
questions.explanation: Both slope equality and area = 0 verify collinearity. Area = (1/2)|1(6-4)+3(4-2)+2(2-6)| = (1/2)|2+6-8| = 0 ✓. Slope AB = 4/2 = 2, BC = 2/1 = 2, AC = 2/1 = 2 ✓.

questions.question: The distance between parallel lines 3x + 4y − 8 = 0 and 3x + 4y + 7 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: Distance between parallel lines ax+by+c₁=0 and ax+by+c₂=0: d = |c₁−c₂|/√(a²+b²) = |−8−7|/√(9+16) = 15/5 = 3.
